96909.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user (on a QA branch, the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit. Everything below is at the same location (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919").
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • An eligible technician at this location, called {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer used by this case only, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Switcher").
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} whose lead technician is {Technician-A}, called {Work-order-A} (for example S1-702).
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} with no lead technician, called {Work-order-B} (for example S1-352).
  • The Work Orders page starts in List (the expected results say List is highlighted at the start).
96909.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top navigation.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Look at the display switcher at the right of the toolbar and hover each of its buttons.
  4. Write down the label or tooltip of each button and which one is highlighted.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  6. Look at which switcher button is highlighted now.
  7. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  8. Look at which switcher button is highlighted now.
  9. In the display switcher, click List (tooltip "List").
96909.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 3 and 4: The switcher offers exactly three display options: List, Tech View and Board View.
  • Steps 4, 6, 8 and 9: Only the option you are viewing is highlighted: List at the start, Tech View after step 5, Board View after step 7, List again after step 9.
  • Step 4: Write down the words you see on each button or tooltip. The design's tooltips read "Table", "By Lead Tech" and "Board". A different label alone is not a fail (the wording is an open product question), but a missing option or no highlight is.

96911.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user (on a QA branch, the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit. Everything below is at the same location (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919").
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • Three eligible technicians at this location: {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard; the expected results use this name, so use exactly this name), {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards; the expected results use this name, so use exactly this name) and {Technician-C} (for example Jenny Wilson). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer named exactly "ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge", called {Customer-A}.
  • A customer named exactly "ZZAUTOTEST Fisquare", called {Customer-B}.
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} whose lead technician is {Technician-A}, called {Work-order-A} (for example S1-702).
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} whose lead technician is {Technician-B}, called {Work-order-B} (for example S1-691).
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} with no lead technician, called {Work-order-C} (for example S1-352). These three are the only Approved work orders for {Customer-A}.
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-B} with any lead, called {Work-order-D}.
  • A search for ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge finds exactly {Work-order-A}, {Work-order-B} and {Work-order-C}, and not {Work-order-D}.
96911.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge.
  4. Open the Status filter, tick Approved (the status the setup gave your test work orders) and close the filter.
  5. In List, write down every work order number shown.
  6. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  7. Write down the work order numbers shown and each group header count.
  8. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  9. Write down the work order numbers on the cards and each column header count.
  10. In the display switcher, click List (tooltip "List").
96911.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 6, 8 and 10: The layout changes straight away on each click, without a page reload.
  • Steps 6 to 10: After every switch the All tab is still selected, the search box still reads ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge and the Status filter still shows the status you ticked.
  • Steps 5, 7 and 9: The same work orders appear in all three displays. With the example data: List shows 3 rows, Tech View shows the same 3 (Unassigned 1 + {Technician-A} 1 + {Technician-B} 1 = 3) and Board View shows the same 3 cards. The ZZAUTOTEST Fisquare work order, {Work-order-D}, appears in none of them.

96912.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user, called {User-A} (on a QA branch, the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit. Everything below is at the same location (for example "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"). {User-A} can be in any display before step 2.
  • A second location that {User-A} is enrolled at, called {Location-B} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Location 2").
  • A second user with Work Orders view who has never changed the display (so still sees List), called {User-B} (for example a Service Advisor), at the first location.
  • A second browser (or another computer).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • An eligible technician at this location, called {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • A customer used by this case only, called {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Follows User").
  • An Approved work order for {Customer-A} whose lead technician is {Technician-A}, called {Work-order-A} (for example S1-702).
96912.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  3. Sign out.
  4. Sign in again as the same user ({User-A}).
  5. Open Work Orders and look at the display.
  6. In the second browser, sign in as the same user ({User-A}).
  7. Open Work Orders and look at the display.
  8. Click your initials at the top right > Change Location and pick {Location-B}.
  9. Open Work Orders and look at the display.
  10. Sign out.
  11. Sign in as {User-B}.
  12. Open Work Orders and look at the display.
96912.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Step 5: After signing in again, Work Orders opens in Board View.
  • Step 7: In the second browser, Work Orders opens in Board View.
  • Step 9: At the second location, Work Orders opens in Board View.
  • Step 12: The second user still sees List: the choice was saved for your user only.

96913.custom_steps:

  2. Click each tab in turn: All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed. For each tab write down which of your three work orders ({Work-order-A}, {Work-order-B}, {Work-order-C}) appear.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  4. Click each tab in turn again and write down which of your three work orders appear under {Technician-A}.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").

96913.expected_head:
Expected results

  • Steps 2, 4 and 6: All four tabs (All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) are shown in every display.
  • Steps 2, 4 and 6: Each tab shows the same work orders in List, Tech View and Board View. With the example data: All shows 3 ({Work-order-A}, {Work-order-B}, {Work-order-C}), Work Orders shows {Work-order-B}, Estimates shows {Work-order-A}, Completed shows {Work-order-C}.
  • Step 1: This case does not check which tab opens first: the default tab was taken out of scope and stays as production has it today.
